Maggie: Ran two nsys captures against the prod-sim cluster (batch=8, seq=2048). Short version: first N requests show big compile/warmup spikes, kernel compile ~100-140ms for a couple ops, kernel-cache miss rate ~29% and it correlates with 95th pct latency cliffs.

Raj: Can you paste the nsys summary? also which kernel names were hot?

Maggie: nsys cmd used: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --output=run1 ./run_infer.sh`. Extracted the following from the timeline: total GPU time stable after warmup, but initial 6 inferences include many `triton::compile` and `cudaLaunchKernel` related stalls. High-level numbers:
- first-compile walltime (sum of compile kernels): ~620ms across 6 calls (avg ~103ms)
- kernel cache miss ratio (unique kernel loads / attempts): ~29%
- tail latency delta during warmup: +18-32% (p50 unchanged)

perf-bot: Auto summary: run1(1782109001) warmup spikes present, run2(1782109465) with --prefetch-kcache lower spikes but still seen.

Li: Timeline snippet looked like: `compile_kernel` entries at t=0.1s, 0.3s, 0.75s then a burst around t=1.2s. Many of those map to fused attention kernels for seq>1024. The compile times are dominated by kernel codegen + JIT linking (text sections).

Sara: FWIW I saw similar with Triton-like backends: cold kernel cache + fragmentation when batching windows are small. If our batching heuristic emits lots of tiny kernels (specialized by seq length and head dim combos) we end up with many permutations and cache churn.

Raj: Do we have a breakdown by kernel signature? i.e., (op,type,seq,batch) -> compile_time. That would help prioritize precompile shapes.

Maggie: I produced a small CSV from the perf extract: `op,seq,batch,compile_ms,count`:
`fused_attn,2048,8,110,6`
`fused_attn,1024,6,85,3`
`matmul,2048,8,40,12`
`softmax,2048,8,18,12`
`kv_cache_write,*,*,12,18`
(The `*` means variable shapes)

Li: That kv_cache_write line is interesting — KV cache write path is doing more memory ops during warmup and can serialize with compile barriers. If the loader path writes full KV at first request, we see memory hotspots on PCIe copy + kernel launches.

Sara: We should test two mitigations: (A) precompile top-N kernel signatures during model load; (B) introduce a warmup request sequence that exercises common sequence lengths so kernels land in cache before user traffic.

Raj: Regarding batching heuristics, current window is 8ms. For seq=2048 the average scheduling-to-launch latency is ~12ms; the small window leads to more specialized kernels because we split batches by arrival patterns. If we increase to 20ms we get larger aggregated batches and fewer distinct kernel variants.

Maggie: I ran an A/B: window=8ms vs 20ms on prod-sim. Results: window=20ms reduced unique kernels by ~22% and reduced compile-related tail by ~9% but increased median scheduling latency by ~1.6ms. Acceptable tradeoff?

Raj: Sounds promising. We should be careful about P99 for interactive endpoints. Maybe adaptive windowing: grow window for seq>1024 or when we detect many cache misses.

Li: Also option to persist kernel cache between containers using hashed keys (model version + op sig + GPU arch). Current behavior ties the cache to instance ephemeral FS. If we persist to shared cache store (object store with LRU) warmups vanish after first job. Need to measure write overhead: storing precompiled blobs ~1.2MB per kernel on avg

Maggie: Measured kernel cache size for this model: ~120MB across ~95 kernels. If we persist, blob store ops on first pull add ~80-120ms once, but subsequent runs zero out compile time.

Sara: Low-risk approach: during model load spawn a background precompile task that touches the hot signatures in a low-priority lane. Uses same code as warmup but doesn't block traffic. That plus small persistent cache should fix most cases.

Raj: Action items: (1) I'll add a flag `--precompile-hot-signatures` and a CI job to generate top-20 shapes from eval traces. (owner: Raj, ETA: Wed) (2) Li will prototype persisting kernel-blob store + eviction policy (owner: Li, ETA: Fri) (3) Maggie to run longer A/B with adaptive batching (owner: Maggie, ETA: Mon)

Maggie: One gotcha — Triton/XLA-like compile times vary with GPU driver + SM arch. On Ampere we saw compile ~110ms, on Hopper sample runs show ~85ms. So we must include arch in cache keys.

perf-bot: Noted. Added tasks to perf board (#perf) and linked trace artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/traces/1782109876_run1.qdrep, 1782109876_run2.qdrep

Li: For next capture let's capture `--sample-interval=5ms` so we can see micro stalls around kernel launches. Also consider `nvtx` annotations from runtime for compile boundaries.

Sara: I'll draft a short doc for warmup best-practices with examples and precompile scripts. Will post to `eng-runtime` channel when done.

Maggie: Thanks everyone. Please ping if you need the raw CSV. I'll attach the small heatmap I generated in a follow-up thread.
